title: Separate two tangled wire clothes hangers
justification: Separating hangers caught together is a familiar laundry recovery. The open hook must be unthreaded around another hanger without dragging it off its support; the distinction is constrained three-dimensional geometry, not labels or an instruction puzzle.
fault: The blue hanger hook encircles the lower crossbar of a hanging white hanger, so a straight pull catches the hook and drags both.
instruction: Separate the tangled hangers and hang the blue one on the empty peg.
objects: Two full-size 40 cm bent steel-wire clothes hangers, 4 mm wire, open hooks
A fixed clothes-rack frame with two perpendicular pegs
skill: Stabilize one hanger while lifting and translating the other through its open hook throat; place the recovered hanger independently on its peg.
scoring: Draft: 0 if a hanger ever leaves the tabletop area or penetrates the other wire; 0.5 once separated with at least 3 cm wire clearance and both released; 1 for blue independently supported on target peg and white on original peg, settled and hands at least 3 cm clear for 3 seconds. All other outcomes 0. Final thresholds will follow validated geometry.

nearest.reason: Linked S-hooks failed occupation category, not a core stocking duty.
Miniature bars omitted hanger hooks and garment manipulation; this task models full-size actual hooks.

risks: Custom bent wire fallback because no SimReady clothes hanger is catalogued; every contact surface must follow visible wire.
Could be considered an occasional nuisance rather than broadly familiar everyday recovery; no occupational importance claim.
Initial interlock must be physically stable, not intersecting or solvable by a plain lift.
Full-size hangers may challenge YAM reach; offline IK and scene trials required.

review.decision: rejected prototype: no full-score contact demo after iterative grasp and approach tests; do not submit
review.novelty: Fresh public index has no accepted/pending hanger disentangling task; checked latest rejection comments 1082 and 1161.
review.feasibility: Physical interlock stable with20mm segment colliders, but YAM wire grasp and bimanual approach not reliable. Left-only corrective approach avoided disturbance but never achieved controlled separation; latest300-step trials both0.0.
